title: A timer you can see from a distance
description: Show the time left as a clear shape, for one person’s session or for a shared classroom display.

blocks.text: A teacher starts the chosen duration, and everyone sees how much is left without reading small digits. For one person’s session the screen means the same thing, but the distance and the viewing conditions are different.

quote.text: I used this timer while I was in school for Dyslexia Therapy! It was a gamer changer, I bought the paid version to be able to make multiple timers without having to change them. I now use this in my kindergarten classroom for different activities and small group interventions!

blocks.text: A shared stretch on one screen

The first version can store a few frequently used durations. The whole shape corresponds to the chosen stretch, the signal is adjustable, and the timer keeps running when the state of the device changes.
Reading the time from where you are

A tool like this has to be tested where it is seen: from a desk or from the other end of the classroom. It is a convenient tool in its own right if the visual representation really does the job; new tasks and rewards are not required for that.
